code-buddy.summary: A multi-agent code-review platform I architected at Qualcomm, used by 12,000+ engineers across 4,000+ repositories.
code-buddy.overview: Code Buddy turns a code change into an actionable review through separate detection, repair, and validation agents. A tool-calling orchestrator retrieves symbols and dependencies, generates candidate fixes, and checks them against guardrails before posting. I architected the platform at Qualcomm and helped scale it to more than two million automated reviews.

cabinai.summary: A seven-agent driving assistant combining driver monitoring, voice, gestures, and local retrieval. Jury Award winner at Qualcomm SparQ 2026.
cabinai.overview: CabinAI connects driver-state perception, location, voice, and hand gestures through a shared orchestration layer. Safety rules and retrieval run locally; a deterministic router can escalate complex requests to cloud models. I built and demonstrated the system solo using a driving simulator, winning the SparQ 2026 Jury Award among 166 teams. The prototype also explores experimental fatigue forecasting.

healthsense.summary: A biosignal dashboard combining ECG classification, signal processing, and an assistant workflow across five sensor streams.
healthsense.overview: HealthSense brings ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG, and motion signals into one experimental interface. Its pipeline combines a small ECG CNN exported to ONNX with signal-processing heuristics and agents that explain the results. I also explored a larger multimodal model and simulated an adaptation workflow. This is an exploratory prototype, with clinical validation and on-device training outside the completed implementation.

cliffside-conquest.summary: A Unity game built around navigating an interactive cliffside environment, with a recorded gameplay walkthrough.
cliffside-conquest.overview: Cliffside Conquest brings character movement and a cliffside game environment together in Unity. The gameplay recording shows the player moving through the scene and interacting with the level. The project combines game programming with environment design and the visual feedback that makes movement readable.

myai.summary: An offline Android assistant with local tools, response caching, and quantized language-model inference through Qualcomm Genie.
myai.overview: MyAI handles simple requests through keyword matching, cached responses, and local tools before invoking a language model. Tools cover calculations, dates, calendar events, contacts, and alarms through structured JSON calls. I tested a quantized Qwen bundle on Snapdragon 8 Elite using Qualcomm Genie. The default APK omits Android’s INTERNET permission, with a build guard to keep it that way.

digital-twin-mapmyindia.summary: A Unity geographic viewer with coordinate-based navigation, location initialization, and animated map transitions.
digital-twin-mapmyindia.overview: Enter a latitude and longitude to fly between locations without losing geographic context. A C# coroutine zooms out, interpolates the map position, and restores the destination zoom. I also worked on location-provider initialization and map controls. The original walkthrough carries the MapMyIndia name; the public implementation uses Mapbox’s Unity SDK.

compiler-construction.summary: A compiler front end in C: twin-buffer lexing, LL(1) parsing, AST construction, symbol tables, and semantic checks.
compiler-construction.overview: Our team built the front end from source characters to structured program information. A DFA lexer feeds a table-driven LL(1) parser using FIRST and FOLLOW sets. The parse tree is reduced to an AST and connected to scope and type information through symbol tables. The implementation includes panic-mode error recovery and partial semantic analysis; executable code generation was not completed.

live-train-status.summary: A Flutter railway app backed by SQL queries for trains, routes, schedules, arrival estimates, and delay updates.
live-train-status.overview: The database models trains, stations, ordered stops, and delays. SQL views and route queries derive possible journeys and arrival estimates; Flutter screens expose train lookup, status information, and administrative delay updates through JSON endpoints. Built as a database-systems course project, the repository preserves the application and schema rather than a currently maintained live railway feed.

florafast-plant-delivery-app.summary: A Flutter plant-shopping app with Firebase sign-in, a product catalog, favorites, and cart interactions.
florafast-plant-delivery-app.overview: FloraFast takes a shopper from browsing plants to viewing products, saving favorites, and building a cart. Firebase Authentication handles email sign-up, sign-in, and password reset. The plant catalog and shopping state use prototype data, while a scan screen explores a future interaction. The walkthrough shows the shopping experience as implemented.

iworkslab-food-delivery-app.summary: A Flutter food-store prototype with shared cart state, product favorites, quantities, and order history.
iworkslab-food-delivery-app.overview: The application connects product browsing, a cart, and order screens through Provider and ChangeNotifier. Adding an item updates quantities and totals across screens, while the orders provider records submitted carts for the order-history view. The implementation uses a local catalog and in-memory state to explore the complete shopping flow.

wisewaterman-water-conservation-game-for.summary: A Unity learning game where a water-powered jetpack and conservation questions turn the lesson into part of play.
wisewaterman-water-conservation-game-for.overview: WiseWaterman challenges players to avoid obstacles while keeping a water-powered jetpack running. Collecting question boxes opens water-conservation challenges; correct answers refill the water meter, while incorrect answers explain the lesson. Built for an NCERT-funded effort overseen by Prof. Neetu Yadav, my contributions covered game design, animation, audio, and writing.

uno-game.summary: A Java Swing UNO game with an object-oriented deck, turn management, and action-card logic.
uno-game.overview: Our team modeled the deck, players, and game state as Java objects and connected them to a Swing interface. Skip, reverse, draw, and wild cards change turn order or the active hand, with validation for permitted moves. The project applies object-oriented design to a familiar game with interacting rules.

igcsm-life-cycle-anaysis.summary: A HoloLens application for exploring life-cycle assessment data, product scenarios, and carbon emissions in mixed reality.
igcsm-life-cycle-anaysis.overview: During DAAD-supported research at TU Braunschweig, our team explored how mixed reality could make life-cycle assessment easier to interpret. The application lets users inspect an e-bicycle, select product scenarios, and compare emissions across its lifetime. I worked on the HoloLens application and interaction flow, collaborating with teams at TU Braunschweig and BITS Pilani and presenting to a scientific jury.

decentralized-academic-certificate-syste.summary: A React, Solidity, and IPFS prototype linking certificate documents to an append-only blockchain registry.
decentralized-academic-certificate-syste.overview: The application separates a document from its registry entry: IPFS stores the file, while a Solidity contract records its hash, metadata, uploader, and timestamp. A React interface connects the upload and lookup workflow through Truffle. The implementation demonstrates content-based verification; institutional issuer accreditation, revocation, and private document access would require further work.

simulation-of-delhi-s-air-pollution.summary: A COMSOL study of vehicle-emission dispersion over a 50 × 50 km Delhi region using an advection-diffusion model.
simulation-of-delhi-s-air-pollution.overview: Our numerical-analysis team modeled how vehicular carbon monoxide disperses under different wind and obstacle conditions. We used COMSOL Multiphysics to solve and visualize the advection-diffusion model, comparing concentration contours over time before applying the setup to a Delhi case study. The report documents the assumptions, numerical setup, and simulation results.

art-gallery.summary: An augmented-reality gallery linking recognized artworks to digital content in the surrounding space.
art-gallery.overview: Built during my AR development work at Invoxel, the gallery uses image recognition to connect physical artworks with spatial digital content. The walkthrough demonstrates the transition from recognizing an image to presenting its related content. It explores how a gallery visit can become an interactive experience through AR.

adoption-app.summary: A Flutter pet-adoption interface with horizontal pet cards, a search field, and nearby and wishlist sections.
adoption-app.overview: An early mobile UI project exploring how to browse pets for adoption. Reusable Flutter widgets compose the greeting, search field, nearby section, and horizontal pet-card lists. The source uses sample pet content and placeholder interactions to develop the layout and component structure, rather than an operating adoption service.

notes-app.summary: A Flutter notes app with Google sign-in, live Firestore updates, and create, edit, and delete workflows.
notes-app.overview: Built during ACM Summer Explore at BITS Pilani, the app connects Firebase Authentication with a Cloud Firestore notes collection. A live snapshot stream updates the note grid, and dedicated screens create, edit, and delete note documents. The project put asynchronous data, account-based navigation, and mobile UI into practice.

other-projects-on-github.summary: More mobile applications, programming coursework, and experiments from my GitHub archive.
other-projects-on-github.overview: My GitHub archive includes smaller Flutter apps, programming exercises, and experiments alongside the projects featured here. These repositories trace my early work with mobile interfaces and application state, followed by larger systems and AI projects. Open the profile to browse their source and documentation.

kxr-smithy-simulation.summary: An immersive workshop simulation built through the Kalipatnapu AR/VR Lab at BITS Pilani.
kxr-smithy-simulation.overview: The smithy simulation translates a workshop process into a virtual environment that users can explore spatially. Built through the Kalipatnapu AR/VR Lab, it combines the workshop scene with an interactive sequence. The recording shows the environment and how the process is presented inside the simulation.

hand-tracking.summary: A spatial-computing prototype exploring hand input as an alternative to conventional controls.
hand-tracking.overview: This prototype uses tracked hands to interact with a virtual scene. The demonstration focuses on the relationship between physical hand movement and the scene’s response, exploring direct interaction without a conventional button-based interface. It is part of my work on AR/VR interaction techniques.

campus-navigation.summary: An AR wayfinding prototype that presents campus-navigation guidance in a spatial interface.
campus-navigation.overview: Campus Navigation explores how route guidance can be presented through an augmented-reality view. The recorded walkthrough demonstrates the navigation flow and how guidance appears in the interface. The project sits at the intersection of location-based applications and spatial interaction.

measure-tape.summary: An augmented-reality measurement prototype for choosing points and displaying a distance in the scene.
measure-tape.overview: Measure Tape brings the interaction of a tape measure into an AR interface. Users choose points in space and see a measurement presented within the scene, as shown in the recording. The project explores point selection and spatial feedback; it is an interface experiment rather than a calibrated measuring instrument.
